jobs.title: Executive Director, Northern California
jobs.description:
If working for an organization that supports the land and people of Israel excites you, then join us and you needn't wait another minute to change the world!

Position Overview:

Jewish National Fund-USA seeks an Executive Director to oversee a multi-million-dollar fundraising campaign across Northern California.
This leadership portfolio includes board and volunteer development and management of the Northern California campaign team. The Executive Director will work with the National Campaign Director to develop and implement fundraising strategies in alignment with the National Annual Campaign Plan.

The Executive Director's main priorities will include expanding Jewish National Fund USA's annual giving through major gifts, general campaign gifts, new donor identification and cultivation, day to day management of operations, and overseeing all aspects of the annual campaign. Building and maintaining strong relationships with existing donors and strategically expanding the fundraising portfolio to support Jewish National Fund USA's growth in Northern California is a paramount priority.

The successful candidate must be an experienced manager and proactive fundraiser who possesses sophisticated leadership and entrepreneurial spirit. The ideal candidate will be collaborative, results-oriented, and passionate for the Jewish National Fund USA mission and Israel. Candidates may come from a variety of backgrounds such as having held a leadership role in the corporate sector, Senior Development Officer or equivalent in a major nonprofit organization, hospital, museum, historical society, major library, or in the academic arena such as a president and/or dean of a college or university. Experience working with or serving on a Board of Directors is essential.

The Executive Director will focus on the cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of high-net worth individuals, foundations and business supporters. The candidate
will also supervise a team of fundraising professionals and, with this team, help enhance Jewish National Fund USA's profile and ensure that the organization is well positioned in a rapidly evolving and competitive environment.

Responsibilities:

Engage in direct and systematic cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of high-net-worth individuals. Direct responsibility for maintaining and building relationships with a portfolio of major gift prospects. Develop strategic annual and long-term fundraising plans and evaluate progress to goals
Steward existing major gift donor relationships; identify and cultivate new major gift donors; renew financial commitments of existing major gift donors
Promote major donor-centric approaches, well-timed solicitation schedules and data-driven program strategy and analysis to increase revenue generation
Foster relationships with financial advisors, attorneys, donors, and other partners who can facilitate the promotion and acquisition of major and planned gifts, bequests, and annuities
Supervise, train, and develop Northern California fundraising staff. Foster a culture of enthusiasm, teamwork, and collaboration among the fundraising team as well as our passionate and committed lay leaders
Build and facilitate philanthropic capacity by maintaining collaborative relations with other organizations throughout Northern California while showcasing Jewish National Fund USA
Work with Northern California leadership to develop Jewish National Fund USA's strategic vision, goal, and strategies and engage committees to assist in the identification, solicitation, and stewardship of current and new donors
Utilize the Jewish National Fund USA Salesforce database to manage donor and prospect relationships
Travel throughout Northern California as needed for donor solicitation and stewardship

Qualifications:

10 years+ of progressive responsibility and experience in fundraising, or proven sales experience in a client-driven business
Extensive experience working with senior-level executives
Strong supervision skills
Significant experience leading and growing successful fundraising/sales functions including building strategies to strengthen and increase funding from a diverse range of sources including individual donors, private corporations, and philanthropic foundations
Excellent decision-making skills and the ability to balance multiple data points, stakeholders, and overall funding landscape in designing and implementing fundraising strategies
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced and collaborative environment, as well as an interest in advancing the organization's fundraising function to be even more strategic, innovative, and results-oriented
Strong communication skills including experience in presenting and public speaking
Strong technical skills and experience with Salesforce preferred or similar CRM/data management system
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience required

Perks:

Days off for all work-prohibitive Jewish holidays, in addition to the secular US holidays
3pm close-of-business on Fridays
Flexible expense reimbursement for mileage and donor meetings
Top-notch healthcare (including dental and vision)
Parental Leave policy
Employer-paid life insurance
Employer-paid short and long-term disability
403(b) with generous 10.5% employer contribution
Opportunities to travel to Israel

Compensation:

$175,000- $200,000

Pay Type:

Salaried

Salaries will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and qualifications for the role.

WHAT WE DO

For 125 years, Jewish National Fund-USA has helped strengthen the land and people of Israel by investing in the communities, infrastructure, and leadership that shape the country’s future. Our work is focused on making Israel’s North and South places where families can build full, vibrant lives with access to medical care, emergency response, water solutions, parks, playgrounds, jobs, and economic opportunity. Working with our donors and partners, we support underpopulated communities, help attract new residents, improve quality of life, and create the conditions for long-term growth. Our work reaches beyond projects on the ground. Through education, travel, and leadership opportunities, we connect Americans of all ages to Israel in meaningful and lasting ways. That vision continues with the World Zionist Village in Be’er Sheva, a global center that will bring people together to live, learn, lead, and strengthen the next generation of Zionist leadership. From urgent relief to long-term transformation, Jewish National Fund-USA is helping build a stronger future for Israel and creating lasting legacies for generations to come. Learn more at jnf.org.

SINCE 1901, JNF HAS:

• Planted more than 250 million trees
• Built over 250 reservoirs and dams
• Developed over 250,000 acres of land
• Created more than 2,000 parks
• Provided the infrastructure for over 1,000 communities
• Connected thousands of children and young adults to Israel and their heritage

Jewish National Fund prides itself on honoring the pioneers of the past and celebrating their spirit by continuing the pioneering tradition in the areas of technology, environmental progress, community development, water renewal and building the land of Israel for many years to come.
Jewish National Fund affirms the bonds of the Jewish family with their strength of unity, the understanding that each member can make a difference and the collective power to build prosperity, develop innovative solutions and promote the greater good.

OUR CREDENTIALS & PARTNERSHIPS

A registered 501(c)(3) organization, Jewish National Fund is recognized as a 4-star organization by Charity Navigator, America's leading independent charity evaluator, for its sound fiscal management, accountability, and transparency. JNF has also been rated a top charity by the American Institute of Philanthropy and meets the 20 rigorous standards of the Better Business Bureau (BBB) Wise Giving Alliance, and the transparency standards of Tzedakah, Inc. No other Jewish organization meets all these standards.

OUR CULTURE

We are Vi Zion
-driven relationship-based, fast-paced, and Positively Israel!

OUR CORE VALUES

Be Bold:
Beyond. We are proud and passionate, vocal, and visionary about Israel and Zionism. We pride ourselves on our out-of-the-box thinking and the great things it accomplishes for the land and with the people of Israel.

Belong:
Stay long. We are an inclusive and diverse workplace welcoming and respecting all cultures, ages, religions, ethnicities, genders, orientations, and physical abilities. Understanding that a work-life balance is crucial to the success of our organization, we are empathetic, understanding, caring, appreciative, and respectful of one another as we strive to develop and retain our professionals and donors for the long-run.
Be Inscribed:
Be the Impact. To walk in the land of Israel and see the impact of our work instills the greatest sense of fulfillment. We strive for each employee to make their mark, leave their footprint, be heard, and feel relevant as together we help ensure the vibrancy of Israel for the next 100 years. We plant the future, not just trees.

Be Kind:
Act with Chesed. At JNF-USA we do not underestimate the power of kindness. We use recognition and praise to motivate teams, individuals, donors, and stakeholders. We are proud of our please and thank you's. We listen and lend a helping hand when a co-worker is challenged. Whether random or deliberate acts, kindness is a key ingredient to our positive workplace and mindset.
B'Yachad:
Together. Great collaboration between our employees, donors and affiliates in Israel is a priority: everyone matters no matter their role. We recognize that open and inspirational communication, teamwork, and collegiality is a force multiplier in reaching our goals, mission, and vision. Jewish National Fund-USA exemplifies the power of unity.

jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
Scion Executive Search
has been retained to conduct an immediate search for a strategic, growth-oriented, and mission-driven Chief Executive Officer on behalf of Vayu Health, an innovative healthcare organization advancing health equity through whole-person care for individuals with complex chronic conditions, behavioral health needs, and significant social determinants of health. This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished executive leader to guide a proven healthcare organization through its next stage of growth, operational scale, and geographic expansion. This position may be performed remotely by candidates with an established California healthcare network, though California-based candidates are strongly preferred. Regular travel throughout California will be expected.

ABOUT VAYU HEALTH

Vayu Health
is a mission-driven healthcare organization redefining how care is delivered to underserved complex individuals living with multiple chronic conditions (with at least uncontrolled diabetes), behavioral health needs, and social needs. Through an innovative, community-based care model, Vayu partners with health plans, providers, and community organizations to improve outcomes for populations that have historically been among the most difficult to serve in traditional healthcare systems.

The organization has established a differentiated model with demonstrated clinical outcomes, secured value-based payer contracts, published research, and a strong financial foundation. With a proven model in place, Vayu is now entering its next phase of organizational growth.

THE OPPORTUNITY:

Vayu Health is at a pivotal crossroads. Having established a proven care model with demonstrated outcomes and burgeoning market traction, the organization is now focused on building the enterprise required to scale that impact across California and beyond.

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Chief Executive Officer will lead Vayu through its next phase of organizational growth and operational maturity. This leader will guide statewide expansion across California while building the scalable infrastructure, strategic partnerships, and organizational capabilities necessary to support long-term growth and position the organization for future expansion into additional geographies and payer environments.

Working in close partnership with Founder Dr. Avni Shah, the CEO will complement Vayu's continued clinical innovation with operational excellence, ensuring the organization's mission, culture, and whole-person approach to care remain at the center of every stage of growth.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Geographic Expansion, Payer Strategy, & Strategic Partnerships

Lead the strategic expansion of Vayu's footprint across California, deepening partnerships with Managed Care Plans (MCPs), providers, and community organizations to extend the organization's reach and impact.
Navigate California's evolving Medi-Cal landscape, including CalAIM and other regulatory and payment reforms, serving as a trusted leader and advocate for Vayu's innovative care model.
Lead the evolution of Vayu's existing and future payer partnerships, innovative payment methods, and contracting strategies, supporting and demonstrating the strength of the organization's whole-person and human centered care model and its ability to improve health outcomes while reducing total cost of care.
Cultivate and strengthen strategic relationships across California's healthcare ecosystem, building executive-level partnerships with health plans, providers, funders, policymakers, and other key stakeholders that advance Vayu's mission and long-term growth.
Develop the long-term strategy for expanding Vayu's care model beyond California, evaluating new markets and growth opportunities while ensuring the organization's operational readiness and financial sustainability.

Operational Infrastructure & Organizational Scale

Build the "Vayu Blueprint" by transforming early-stage startup processes into scalable, enterprise-grade operating systems that support sustainable organizational growth.
Design and implement the operational infrastructure, technology, and AI-enabled workflows necessary to improve efficiency, strengthen execution, and reduce administrative burden while preserving Vayu's human-centered model of care.
Establish repeatable systems, processes, and organizational capabilities that enable Vayu to scale without compromising clinical quality, patient outcomes, or organizational culture.
Build an operational foundation that enables Vayu's care model to scale across California today while positioning the organization for future geographic expansion and broader payer portability.

Financial Strategy & Organizational Sustainability

Lead Vayu's long-term financial strategy, ensuring the organization's growth strengthens its financial position through disciplined P&L management, sound unit economics, and operational efficiencies that reduce the cost of care as the organization scales.
Champion Vayu's long-term sustainability by securing the capital and strategic partnerships needed to support organizational growth, while advancing a balanced funding model that includes earned revenue, value-based payer partnerships, grants, and strategic philanthropy.
Serve as a trusted executive partner to health plans, providers, funders, and government stakeholders, articulating the value of Vayu's innovative care model through measurable outcomes, rigorous outcomes and ROI analysis, and a deep understanding of the intersection between clinical delivery, payment models, actuarial science, and healthcare policy.

Clinical Partnership & Care Model Excellence

Partner closely with clinical leadership to ensure Vayu's care model continues to deliver exceptional patient outcomes while operating with the efficiency and discipline required to support sustainable growth.
Balance whole-person and human centered care with sound operational and financial stewardship as the organization scales.
Partner closely with Founder Dr. Avni Shah to translate visionary clinical innovation into scalable operational execution, ensuring the integrity, quality, and heart of Vayu's care model remain central as the organization grows.

People, Culture, & Organizational Leadership

Lead, inspire, and develop a rapidly growing organization, fostering organizational clarity, accountability, mission alignment, and transparent communication through periods of sustained growth and change.
Build and mentor a high-performing leadership team capable of supporting Vayu's continued growth while reinforcing a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous learning.
Cultivate a culture that prioritizes the human on both sides of the care equation, investing in employee engagement, professional agency, and leadership development while reducing administrative burden through thoughtful systems and operational excellence.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Required Qualifications

Executive Leadership:
7+ years of executive leadership experience (CEO, COO, Executive Director, SVP, or equivalent) within a healthcare delivery organization, healthcare services organization, or growth-stage healthcare enterprise.
Proven Scaling Record:
Demonstrated success leading a healthcare delivery organization or tech-enabled healthcare service through a significant period of growth, transformation, or operational scaling, including experience managing multi-site operations, complex organizations with budgets of $10M+ or teams of 25+ employees.
California Health System Expertise:
Deep understanding of California's Medi-Cal ecosystem, Managed Care Plans (MCPs), reimbursement models, and evolving regulatory landscape.
Financial & Philanthropic Acumen:
Demonstrated financial leadership, including P&L oversight, unit economics, sustainable revenue strategy, payer contracting, and diversified funding models. Experience securing strategic partnerships, transformational capital, grants, and strategic philanthropy, with the ability to engage effectively with Boards, funders, grantors, and philanthropic partners.
Infrastructure Mindset:
Experience building scalable operating systems and infrastructure designed for replication, including multi-site healthcare operations, technology-enabled service models, or EMR-enabled clinical environments.
Nonprofit Governance:
Significant experience partnering with nonprofit Boards of Directors, supporting governance, and managing complex grant-funded or mission-driven organizations.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading healthcare delivery, value-based care, or organizational expansion across multiple states.
Experience working alongside founders or within founder-led organizations during transition periods.
Experience leveraging AI, emerging technologies, and digital innovation to improve operational scalability, care delivery, and organizational effectiveness.
Experience engaging with healthcare policy, government relations, or industry advocacy efforts at the state or national level.
Experience partnering closely with clinical leaders and multidisciplinary care teams, with an appreciation for balancing clinical excellence with operational and financial performance.
Experience applying human-centered design principles to healthcare delivery, patient experience, organizational development, or service innovation.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

This position offers a competitive base salary range of $275,000 – $315,000, commensurate with experience, along with a comprehensive benefits package.

APPLICATIONS AND NOMINATIONS:

Vayu Health has retained the services of Scion Executive Search, a national executive search firm specializing in nonprofit recruitment, to assist in conducting this important search. For immediate consideration, please apply with your resume and cover letter, formatted in Microsoft Word, via: https://scionexecutivesearch.com/job/14895.

As the leading global type 1 diabetes (T1D) research and advocacy organization, Breakthrough T1D helps make everyday life with T1D better while driving toward cures. We invest in the most promising research to turn ideas into life-changing therapies and devices. We work with government, regulatory officials, and insurance companies to address issues that impact the T1D community -- breaking through barriers that limit access to care worldwide. We provide resources and guidance that makes it easier to live and thrive with T1D. This is more than a moment -- we're empowering a movement for the T1D community. Share your support and help educate and empower individuals facing type 1 diabetes.

Our mission is to improve lives today and tomorrow by accelerating life changing breakthroughs to treat, prevent and ultimately, cure T1D and its complications. Always, we are guided by a single purpose: As we drive towards curing type 1 diabetes, we help make everyday life better for the people who face it.

The Development Director (DD) at Breakthrough T1D is integral in the day-to-day execution of integrated fundraising efforts to support our organizational strategy and mission. Their relationships with constituents and donors on behalf of Breakthrough T1D will ensure the expansion of our reach to support maximum chapter and event growth to further our mission.

The Development Director role focuses on relationship building with key donors and fundraising volunteers within their assigned event portfolio, driving impact and strengthening both donor and volunteer pipeline resulting in increased revenue and results.

This individual is a high-impact, high-energy team player who can effectively bring the mission to life within the community through collaboration, cultivation, inspiration, and engagement. They will implement activities to support organizational strategies in their assigned chapter to drive optimal results and actively demonstrate and promote enterprise-wide mindsets. They will lead our Orange County Gala and play an instrumental role with corporate development and mid-level giving for the chapter. This individual will have two (2) direct reports.

As one of the top performing territories in the country, the Southern California and Hawaii territory plays a vital role in the organization’s success. The So CA & HI territory has 18 staff, 3 Chapter Boards and 13 events collectively driving over $10.1 million in total net revenue and $4.91M in total event net revenue

We have a hybrid work schedule, in office, working remotely, and in the field.

Key Responsibilities

Fundraising & Engagement – 60%

In collaboration with national and chapter partners, create and implement annual strategies that will drive growth of assigned event portfolio through corporate and individual donor engagement and stewardship at the chapter level. Identify and develop new business with existing donors and new prospects.

Acquire, cultivate, and solicit mid and major level Fund A Cure donors

Volunteer Management – 20%

Recruit, cultivate, and manage volunteer leaders that drive revenue as key partners; includes event leadership and committees
Ensure meaningful engagement of volunteers at all levels and engage in good working relationships with key volunteer partners.
Partner with volunteer leadership to solicit funding and other support from individuals, corporations, foundations and other sources of funding and/or influence.

Maintain departmental and organization-wide policies and procedures

Strong skills in the identification, cultivation, solicitation, and on-going stewardship of donors and supporters.
In the Signature Events/gala space a history of securing and retaining table hosts, guests, event sponsors and donors.
Experience partnering with strong and active volunteer leaders, including working successfully with a large network of passionate volunteers.
Demonstrate a high degree of energy, integrity, courage, empathy, and creativity. High emotional IQ. Superior active listening, analytical, and critical thinking skills. A team player who can achieve individual objectives and support those of the entire chapter team.

Leadership Development Track

DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS

An incredibly exciting opportunity for an experienced NYC restaurant operator to join a highly successful, growing healthy QSR / fast-casual restaurant group
at a pivotal moment in its expansion.

This is not an early-stage concept still trying to figure things out. The business is successful, well positioned for growth and has already built a strong corporate foundation around its restaurants. Key leadership functions are in place, the company operates with a modern, technology-driven approach, and there is a significant pipeline for additional locations.
Now they are looking for an exceptional Director of Operations
who can take ownership of restaurant operations, develop the next generation of leaders and help build the infrastructure necessary to scale.
The role reports directly to the CEO and sits alongside the company's existing HQ leadership team. As the right person grows into the position, the goal is for the DOO to take increasing ownership of operations, allowing the CEO to focus more heavily on strategy and future growth.

THE OPPORTUNITY

We are looking for much more than someone who can manage multiple restaurants.
The ideal candidate is a builder
— someone who has experienced restaurant growth firsthand, understands what it takes to open successful new locations and knows how to create systems that make a growing organization stronger rather than more complicated.
You'll oversee and develop General Managers, Kitchen Managers and other restaurant leaders while creating the structure needed for future Area / Regional leadership.
You'll help strengthen SOPs, training programs, reporting, communication and accountability across the organization. You'll be deeply involved in new openings and help make sure the company has the right people, systems and standards in place before each new restaurant opens its doors.
The company is specifically looking for someone who can turn its successful operating model into a repeatable playbook for growth
, without sacrificing food quality, culture or performance along the way.

THE PERFECT BACKGROUND: QSR + FULL-SERVICE NYC HOSPITALITY

This is probably the most important part of the profile.
We would love to find someone who has worked successfully in both QSR / fast-casual and full-service restaurants, ideally in New York City.

From the QSR world, you understand systems, efficiency, technology, labor, KPIs, high-volume execution, standardization and scalability.

But your full-service background means you also understand something equally important:
Hospitality is about people.

You love restaurants. You enjoy being around teams. You know how to motivate a GM, recognize emerging talent and build a culture where people want to perform and grow.
You can analyze a P&L and build an SOP, but you're equally comfortable walking into a busy restaurant, connecting with the team and understanding within 20 minutes what's really happening in the operation.
We don't want someone who manages restaurants exclusively through spreadsheets and dashboards.
We want a restaurant person who also happens to be an exceptional business operator.

BUILD TEAMS. OPEN RESTAURANTS. SCALE THE BUSINESS.

A major part of this opportunity will be supporting the company's continued NYC expansion.
We're especially interested in candidates who have opened multiple restaurants and helped scale a growing restaurant group
— someone who understands that opening locations isn't simply about construction schedules and opening checklists.
It's about people.
Who will run the next restaurant? Who on today's team can become tomorrow's GM? Which GM has the potential to become an Area Leader? How early do we hire and train new managers? How do we make sure every new location delivers the same standards without losing its hospitality?
You'll help answer those questions while building the leadership pipeline behind the company's growth.
The current expansion plan calls for additional NYC locations through 2027, making this an opportunity to have a meaningful impact on the company's next generation of restaurants.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN
Multi-unit restaurant operations and performance
Development and coaching of GMs and restaurant leadership
New restaurant openings and operational readiness
P&L, labor, food cost, budgeting and forecasting
SOPs and scalable operational systems
Manager training and leadership development
Restaurant KPIs, reporting and performance analysis
Operational audits and continuous improvement
Succession planning and internal talent development
Cross-functional collaboration with CEO and HQ leadership
Building the infrastructure needed for continued expansion

One of the best ways to describe the company's philosophy for this role is simple: your success should be measured by what happens when you're not in the building.

The goal is to develop managers into confident, accountable leaders who can independently run excellent restaurants.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR
The ideal candidate brings 7+ years of progressive multi-unit restaurant operations experience
, with a strong preference for someone who understands the NYC market.
You should have a track record of scaling restaurant operations, opening new locations, developing strong GMs and building systems that actually work in restaurants.

We're particularly interested in someone with:
Experience across both QSR / fast casual and full-service restaurants

Strong multi-unit NYC restaurant experience
Multiple successful new restaurant openings
Excellent P&L and financial acumen
Experience building SOPs, training programs and scalable systems
Strong understanding of restaurant technology and performance metrics
A track record of developing and promoting leaders
Excellent communication and organizational skills
Genuine passion for hospitality and people
The ability to balance high standards with a positive, collaborative leadership style

Experience with franchising or preparing a restaurant company for larger-scale expansion would be a strong plus.

COMPENSATION & GROWTH
Base Salary: $160,000–$180,000

Target Total Compensation: $180,000–$200,000
, including a performance-based bonus program tied to clear, measurable goals.
Additional benefits include a $1,000 monthly healthcare stipend, Paid Time Off, complimentary meals and leadership development opportunities.

Most importantly, this role has a clear pathway toward Vice President of Operations
as the company continues to expand.

WHY THIS ROLE?
Because this is the sweet spot for an ambitious operator.
The company is already successful and has the leadership, resources and momentum to grow — but it's still at a stage where the person joining today can have a real influence on what the organization looks like tomorrow.
The systems you build can become the company's future playbook. The managers you develop can become its next generation of leaders. And the restaurants you help open can become the foundation for much bigger growth.
If you bring the discipline of QSR, the hospitality instincts of full-service restaurants, and a genuine love for building teams and opening restaurants
, this could be an exceptional next chapter in your career.

Mission of the Daniel Murphy Scholarship Fund 

The Daniel Murphy Scholarship Fund (DMSF) unlocks educational opportunities for talented Chicago-area students facing financial need. We partner with Scholars, families, schools, alumni, donors, and community leaders through high school and beyond by providing scholarships, academic programs and personal support so that each Scholar can reach their full potential. 

Founded by the Murphy brothers in 1989, DMSF now offers around 150 scholarships to 8th graders each year, supporting more than 500 Scholars in high school with a 100% graduation rate. Those Scholars are attending roughly 40 different parochial and independent day schools in the Chicago area, as well as 40 boarding schools from coast to coast. For more information, please visit www.dmsf.org.

Position Overview 

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) serves as a key member of the executive leadership team and strategic partner to DMSF’s CEO. The COO is responsible for leading and strengthening organizational operations, managing and supporting the Development team, driving cross-functional disciplined execution of strategic priorities, and helping advance DMSF’s mission through strong operational leadership, and donor engagement support.

The COO works closely with the CEO on strategic planning, fundraising initiatives, board engagement, donor strategy, and organizational development, ensuring that systems, people, and priorities are aligned to maximize impact.

Assist in managing organizational priorities and ensuring follow-through on key initiatives.

Summary

The Deputy Director of Engineering (DDOE)
is responsible for planning, prioritizing, communi-cating, and executing the engineering work efforts across Trident Research to ensure engineer-ing products and services are delivered on time and within scope. The DDOE works under the oversight of the Director of Engineering (DOE) to manage engineering tasking across multiple disciplines, including Mechanical, Electrical, Software, and Systems, as well as aerospace and materials engineering where applicable, ensuring on-time and on-budget completion of R&D-focused work that prioritizes high-quality, practical solutions over perfection. The greatest resource at Trident Research is our engineering talent, and the DDOE is the frontline manager of this multidisciplinary team. It is, therefore, critical to mentor and coach each team member to achieve individual and team success. The DDOE fosters a healthy, trusting, and growth-ori-ented environment through direct engagement with engineers, aligning with the DOE’s vision for a cohesive engineering team. We recognize our work is R&D in nature in many cases and per-fection is never the goal. To build a healthy team, development of a trusting and growth-oriented environment through engagement with the engineers is key. 

DDOE works closely with the Director of Engineering (DOE) to proactively search for, review, and ultimately recommend new technologies, tools, equipment, and other engineering resources that are ‘right for Trident’ and are reasonable (e.g., business case is sound). The DDOE collaborates with the DOE and the Head of Technology and Research (HTR) to identify and resolve technically challenging aspects of the work and recommend technology investments. While it is the responsibility of the DOE to submit and coordinate with the Executive Team to ensure needs are budgeted and executed accordingly, the DDOE does serve as the eyes and ears for the engineers on the floor to make sure we’re properly resourced to complete the work. 

The DDOE will participate in the full cycle of engineering development, from identifying, recruiting, and training talent through overseeing and engaging on engineering design reviews, to rep-resenting Trident Research in presenting developed solutions and product results to our customers. The DDOE supports the DOE in all phases of the engineering development cycle, ensuring alignment with the DOE’s vision and corporate objectives. A principal goal of the DDOE is the appropriate execution of the Systems Engineering Process (SEP) for the work to be accomplished for the company. The DDOE implements the SEP under DOE oversight, ensuring the use of agile development methodologies to support rapid prototyping and iterative development of minimum viable products. Sound engineering principles are required of all engineers if the team is to be successful, and the DDOE's greatest influence in this regard is the company SEP. 

The DDOE works in partnership with the Program Management Office (PMO). Our Project Man-agers (PMs) are responsible for supervising projects, staying on budget, and are directly accountable to our customers. The DDOE and PMs work together to ensure that Trident tracks and delivers exceptional engineering products and services that meet or exceed customer expectations and contractual requirements. The DDOE coordinates with PMs to resolve programmatic conflicts, communicate delays, and ensure technical excellence in contracted efforts, un-der DOE oversight. It is expected that the DDOE will expend approximately half of their time directly engaged on helping to lead, refine, and ensure technical excellence across all contracted work. 

 Success in this position will require proactive communication (i.e., delays, issues, JIRA tasking, etc.). The DDOE must be a strategic thinker and problem solver, possess outstanding technical engineering skills (particularly with regards to risk management), demonstrate excellent written and oral communications skills when representing the company, and be self-motivated to engage and lead. The DDOE ensures engineering processes are effective and efficient, contributing to the DOE’s vision of intuitive and adaptable processes.

 The DDOE must also have prior experience and demonstrated expertise in conducting research and leading technical teams, technical staff supervision, coaching and mentoring, conflict resolution and career mentoring in a rapid-paced research and development environment. The DDOE helps define positional responsibilities and metrics for engineers with the DOE. The met-rics should roll up into department KRAs and KPIs that are ultimately approved by the president. 

Requirements

Educational and Experience Requirements:

●      Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering Required, a Master of Science or doctorate degree in engineering or related field preferred
●      5 years minimum engineering experience
●      Proven track record of leading world-class engineers in multiple disciples.
●      Experience setting and meeting budget/time goals for project tasking utilizing JIRA .
●      Command leadership skills demonstrating sound judgement and personal accountability, with a commitment to excellence, commitment to mission, and commitment to the team.
●      Excellence in Microsoft Office, Project, and SharePoint products, and Jira required.
●      Experience providing written and oral presentations to internal and external customers.
●      Experience in integrating AI, machine learning (ML), and data analytics into engineering solutions, ensuring robust, secure, and optimized models for edge deployment. 
●      Experience in exploring new technologies and methodologies for military applications, ensuring systems are modular, scalable, and adaptable to evolving threats. 

Other Requirements:

●      Must obtain and maintain a minimum of a Secret Security Clearance
●      Must obtain and maintain a valid passport
●      Occasionally exposed to disagreeable conditions. May work extended hours or weekends. May travel overnight or on weekends.

Key Responsibilities
Engineering Team Leadership 50% 1.   Provide effective day-to-day programmatic resource allocation to the engineering team such that all engineering team members are performing optimally.
2.   Provide consistent and frequent feedback to employees by conducting 1-on-1 meetings with direct reports at least biweekly (travel permitting). These sessions are meant to provide mentoring and coaching on work products as well as engagement on work satisfaction, growth opportunities and personal connection within the team.
3.   Provide at least one threads comment per direct report per month.
4.   Identify training plan and career growth track for each direct report semi-annually.
5.   Maintain a record of your team’s skill. Update at least semi-annually.
6.   Monitor and update job descriptions semi-annually for your team members as necessary so that the appropriate duties and responsibilities are captured. This should be done in advance of performance reviews.
7.   Consistently issue and monitor work tasking so that each team member has ample direction and work for a two week time period. Adjustments to priorities can be made, but we must ensure that all team members are engaged.
8.   Work is to be peer reviewed by engineering personnel prior to delivery to the PM to ensure efforts are completed and without error. Draw lessons learned and adjust follow-on tasks accordingly. 
9.   Work with HR and management to execute staff hiring, counseling, or terminations as necessary to create a stellar team. Do not avoid difficult conversations which can create disharmony in the team.
10. Invest time in understanding the latest technology advances within your scope to recommend investments where possible to advance the company’s capabilities.
11. Provide recommendations on team processes, procedures, tools, resources, and facilities improvements to DOE for corporate investment when requested by DOF & ET annually (October) and as needed throughout the year.
12. Perform formal performance evaluations for each team member at least twice per year, highlighting specific accomplishments on specific tasking and identifying areas where improvement can be obtained or where new skills will be required for future envisioned work tasking. Include a candid discussion on personal goals and ensure those are captured and reviewed.
13. Report tasking progress at each milestone to the DOE, ensuring lessons learned are drawn and follow-on tasks are adjusted accordingly.
14. Contribute to the integration of AI, machine learning, and data analytics into sensor systems for real-time data processing, predictive maintenance, and autonomous decision-making under DOE guidance.
15. Support the exploration of new technologies and methodologies for military applications, ensuring systems are modular, scalable, and adaptable under DOE oversight.

Department and Cross-Department Communication 20% 1.   Communications with PM’s: verify work is being completed effectively on-time and within scope, reporting of any potential or know delays, negotiation of hours and scope on tasking, etc. 
2.   Coordinate with PMs to resolve programmatic conflicts, such as resource allocation or schedule adjustments, and communicate delays promptly to ensure contract compliance and customer satisfaction under DOE oversight.
3.   Cross Department Communication – DDOE often must communicate with other departments inside of Trident. Communication should be respectful and timely so that all departments have the information they need in order to meet their respective objectives.

Jira Management 30% 1.   Allocate resources in Jira to effectively complete the work on-time

3.   Enter project Epic level tasks with estimates as allocated in the PMO EP
4.   Communication with engineering team members regarding Jira tasking being updated according to the work being completed

Executive Director, National Capital Region (NCR) Chapter

Blue Star Families

Blue Star Families is the largest nonprofit dedicated to making military life better for families. Each year, we support over 1.5 million military- and veteran-connected family members through a national network of 300,000+ members and local chapters in communities across the country.

Our mission is simple and bold: We make military life awesome for families.

We listen, share, partner, and act to deliver evidence-based, data-driven solutions that work for real people. We’re a lifestyle organization, a friend and neighbor, and a trusted partner. Our approach is collaborative, human-centered, and designed with the whole family in mind.

A Blue Star Family is one with an immediate family member — a spouse, parent, or child — actively serving in the U.S. Armed Forces, including the Guard and Reserves. These families face unique challenges: frequent relocations, deployments, career disruption, and isolation. We respond with research-informed programs that create connection, build resilience, and foster a true sense of belonging.

We serve with urgency but build trust over time — because change happens at the speed of trust. Whether we’re driving spouse employment, supporting caregivers, or helping communities welcome military families, we strive for upstream solutions.

Who We’re Looking For

Bold thinkers. Fast movers. Smart collaborators. People who want to build, lead, and drive measurable change — and who care deeply about making an impact that matters.

What You’ll Do Here

Solve complex challenges with data, heart, and humility
Build cross-sector partnerships that get things done
Help military families feel at home wherever they live

If you're ready to work in a high-performance, mission-driven environment — and to make life better for those who serve — Blue Star Families is where you belong.

General Description

The Executive Director (ED) is the senior-most leader of Blue Star Families' National Capital Region (NCR) Chapter — the organization's flagship chapter, with 30,000+ members and the largest volunteer base in the network. Reporting to the VP of Chapter Impact & Outposts, the ED owns local strategy, revenue growth, community impact, and team performance, overseeing staff, volunteers, budget, fundraising, programs, and long-term chapter sustainability.

Because the Chapter is based in Washington, DC, this ED carries responsibilities unique among BSF Executive Directors: cultivating relationships with political and government figures, representing BSF on Capitol Hill, serving as the Chapter's primary liaison to BSF's National Headquarters, and standing in for the CEO and President at high-visibility DC engagements when needed. Given the Chapter's scale and visibility, the ED is expected to grow annual revenue to a sustained seven-figure ($1M+) level, building a funding model that matches the Chapter's national profile.

This is BSF's most externally visible chapter ED role — ideal for a high-capacity executive skilled in strategic partnerships, six-figure fundraising, board leadership, and cross-functional coordination, who delivers the mission with excellence, inclusion, and measurable outcomes.

As a fully remote organization, BSF relies on periodic in-person gatherings (staff offsites, retreats, company-wide events) that require overnight travel several times a year; participation is a core part of the role. The ED must also travel frequently within the DC metro area for Hill visits, HQ meetings, and events.

The Executive Director must reside in, or have at least three years of residence in or significant knowledge of, the Washington, DC metro/DMV region, and must be willing to relocate to the Chapter location.

Key Job Functions

Government Affairs & National Headquarters Relations

Cultivate and leverage relationships with members of Congress, congressional staff, Administration officials, and other political figures on BSF's behalf; represent BSF at Hill briefings, hearings, and events to advance policy priorities for military and veteran families.
Serve as the Chapter's primary liaison to BSF's National Headquarters, coordinating chapter activity with national strategy; stand in for the CEO and President at high-visibility DC meetings and events when needed.
Partner with BSF's Policy, Government Relations, and Executive Office teams to ensure unified messaging, exercising sound political judgment given the visibility and sensitivity of this work.

Fundraising & Revenue Leadership

Develop and execute a Chapter Sustainability Plan with a clear pathway to $1M+ in annual revenue, reflecting the DC donor landscape and NCR's flagship scale.
Secure major gifts from corporations, foundations, and high-net-worth individuals, prioritizing DC-based government contractors, trade associations, and national corporate headquarters; own annual fundraising goals and donor stewardship.
Diversify revenue through corporate sponsorships, foundations, workplace giving, government opportunities, and community campaigns, partnering with the Development and National teams on strategy and pipeline.

Executive Leadership & Chapter Operations

Lead the Chapter's full operational portfolio — staff, volunteers, programs, budget, and partnerships — the largest such portfolio in the BSF network.
Recruit, manage, coach, and develop chapter staff and its large-scale volunteer corps, and serve as BSF's senior representative in the region, upholding a high standard of professionalism and visibility with media, policymakers, and national partners.
Ensure excellence in national program execution (Welcome Week, MFLS, Nourish the Service, etc.), apply BSF's data-driven evaluation model, and maintain compliance with operational policies, budgets, KPIs, and risk management.

Advisory Board & Stakeholder Engagement

Recruit, develop, and steward a strategic local Advisory Board, intentionally including political, government, and national-security-adjacent representation.
Cultivate relationships with VIPs, elected officials, military installation leaders, philanthropic champions, and corporate executives, leveraging these relationships to advance BSF's priorities and regional presence.
Represent BSF at community events and national-level convenings, including Hill events and high-visibility engagements on behalf of the CEO and President.

Community Building & Cross-Sector Partnerships

Establish the ED as a recognized thought leader on military family issues, building a network of civic, military, corporate, nonprofit, and philanthropic partners, with emphasis on DC's concentration of federal agencies and defense-sector organizations.
Serve as the Chapter's chief ambassador for military-connected families using MFLS insights and BSF research, including with congressional and government audiences; identify opportunities for regional expansion and innovative programming.

Communications & Brand Stewardship

Deepen BSF's local presence through storytelling and brand-consistent communications, partnering with Marketing/Comms to amplify Chapter impact.
Serve as an articulate public voice for military families, including in settings representing the CEO and President.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Required Experience, Skills & Background

Bachelor's degree or 7+ years of progressively responsible experience in community development, nonprofit leadership, or strategic partnerships; 5+ years of staff management experience.
Proven six-figure fundraising success, with experience building toward seven-figure organizational revenue strongly preferred; demonstrated success growing an organization or major initiative.
Demonstrated experience working with Congress, government agencies, or political campaigns, with an established (or rapidly buildable) network of political and governmental relationships in Washington, DC.
Exceptional executive communication skills, with comfort representing senior executives (CEO/President-level) in high-visibility settings; experience managing an advisory board or similar governance structure.
Strong organizational management skills — budgeting, planning, KPI accountability, and team development — ideally at the scale of a large, multi-site or high-membership organization.
Sound political judgment and discretion, with the ability to navigate bipartisan relationships professionally; mission-driven mindset with integrity, humility, and emotional intelligence.
Willingness to work nights/weekends for essential community events (<25% overnight travel, plus frequent local Hill/HQ travel); ability to lift/carry supplies and equipment up to 30 lbs.

Desired Experience, Skills & Background

Experience using CRM systems; Salesforce a plus.
Understanding of military culture and the lived experience of military families; knowledge of the BSF ecosystem and programs.
Prior experience on Capitol Hill, in a government affairs role, at a national trade association, or in a federal agency.
Existing relationships with DC-based corporate, philanthropic, or government funders.

More About Blue Star Families

Blue Star Families empowers military and Veteran families to thrive by connecting them with their civilian neighbors — both people and organizations — to create strong communities of mutual support. We believe we're all stronger when we take care of one another.

Our groundbreaking research is raising the nation's awareness of the unique challenges of military family life. With the help of neighbors across the country, Blue Star Families is overcoming the isolation and alienation of frequent moves, deployments, and reduced support from the government. Our innovative programs are solving specific challenges for military families, including fighting economic insecurity with resources that foster spouse career development, creating family strength with rich family programming, and providing critical peer support for caregivers, whose numbers are only increasing.

Scion Executive Search
has been retained to conduct an immediate search for a strategic, growth-oriented, and mission-driven Chief Executive Officer on behalf of Vayu Health, an innovative healthcare organization advancing health equity through whole-person care for individuals with complex chronic conditions, behavioral health needs, and significant social determinants of health. This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished executive leader to guide a proven healthcare organization through its next stage of growth, operational scale, and geographic expansion. This position may be performed remotely by candidates with an established California healthcare network, though California-based candidates are strongly preferred. Regular travel throughout California will be expected.

ABOUT VAYU HEALTH

Vayu Health
is a mission-driven healthcare organization redefining how care is delivered to underserved complex individuals living with multiple chronic conditions (with at least uncontrolled diabetes), behavioral health needs, and social needs. Through an innovative, community-based care model, Vayu partners with health plans, providers, and community organizations to improve outcomes for populations that have historically been among the most difficult to serve in traditional healthcare systems.

The organization has established a differentiated model with demonstrated clinical outcomes, secured value-based payer contracts, published research, and a strong financial foundation. With a proven model in place, Vayu is now entering its next phase of organizational growth.

THE OPPORTUNITY:

Vayu Health is at a pivotal crossroads. Having established a proven care model with demonstrated outcomes and burgeoning market traction, the organization is now focused on building the enterprise required to scale that impact across California and beyond.

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Chief Executive Officer will lead Vayu through its next phase of organizational growth and operational maturity. This leader will guide statewide expansion across California while building the scalable infrastructure, strategic partnerships, and organizational capabilities necessary to support long-term growth and position the organization for future expansion into additional geographies and payer environments.

Working in close partnership with Founder Dr. Avni Shah, the CEO will complement Vayu's continued clinical innovation with operational excellence, ensuring the organization's mission, culture, and whole-person approach to care remain at the center of every stage of growth.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Geographic Expansion, Payer Strategy, & Strategic Partnerships

Lead the strategic expansion of Vayu's footprint across California, deepening partnerships with Managed Care Plans (MCPs), providers, and community organizations to extend the organization's reach and impact.
Navigate California's evolving Medi-Cal landscape, including CalAIM and other regulatory and payment reforms, serving as a trusted leader and advocate for Vayu's innovative care model.
Lead the evolution of Vayu's existing and future payer partnerships, innovative payment methods, and contracting strategies, supporting and demonstrating the strength of the organization's whole-person and human centered care model and its ability to improve health outcomes while reducing total cost of care.
Cultivate and strengthen strategic relationships across California's healthcare ecosystem, building executive-level partnerships with health plans, providers, funders, policymakers, and other key stakeholders that advance Vayu's mission and long-term growth.
Develop the long-term strategy for expanding Vayu's care model beyond California, evaluating new markets and growth opportunities while ensuring the organization's operational readiness and financial sustainability.

Operational Infrastructure & Organizational Scale

Build the "Vayu Blueprint" by transforming early-stage startup processes into scalable, enterprise-grade operating systems that support sustainable organizational growth.
Design and implement the operational infrastructure, technology, and AI-enabled workflows necessary to improve efficiency, strengthen execution, and reduce administrative burden while preserving Vayu's human-centered model of care.
Establish repeatable systems, processes, and organizational capabilities that enable Vayu to scale without compromising clinical quality, patient outcomes, or organizational culture.
Build an operational foundation that enables Vayu's care model to scale across California today while positioning the organization for future geographic expansion and broader payer portability.

Financial Strategy & Organizational Sustainability

Lead Vayu's long-term financial strategy, ensuring the organization's growth strengthens its financial position through disciplined P&L management, sound unit economics, and operational efficiencies that reduce the cost of care as the organization scales.
Champion Vayu's long-term sustainability by securing the capital and strategic partnerships needed to support organizational growth, while advancing a balanced funding model that includes earned revenue, value-based payer partnerships, grants, and strategic philanthropy.
Serve as a trusted executive partner to health plans, providers, funders, and government stakeholders, articulating the value of Vayu's innovative care model through measurable outcomes, rigorous outcomes and ROI analysis, and a deep understanding of the intersection between clinical delivery, payment models, actuarial science, and healthcare policy.

Clinical Partnership & Care Model Excellence

Partner closely with clinical leadership to ensure Vayu's care model continues to deliver exceptional patient outcomes while operating with the efficiency and discipline required to support sustainable growth.
Balance whole-person and human centered care with sound operational and financial stewardship as the organization scales.
Partner closely with Founder Dr. Avni Shah to translate visionary clinical innovation into scalable operational execution, ensuring the integrity, quality, and heart of Vayu's care model remain central as the organization grows.

People, Culture, & Organizational Leadership

Lead, inspire, and develop a rapidly growing organization, fostering organizational clarity, accountability, mission alignment, and transparent communication through periods of sustained growth and change.
Build and mentor a high-performing leadership team capable of supporting Vayu's continued growth while reinforcing a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous learning.
Cultivate a culture that prioritizes the human on both sides of the care equation, investing in employee engagement, professional agency, and leadership development while reducing administrative burden through thoughtful systems and operational excellence.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Required Qualifications

Executive Leadership:
7+ years of executive leadership experience (CEO, COO, Executive Director, SVP, or equivalent) within a healthcare delivery organization, healthcare services organization, or growth-stage healthcare enterprise.
Proven Scaling Record:
Demonstrated success leading a healthcare delivery organization or tech-enabled healthcare service through a significant period of growth, transformation, or operational scaling, including experience managing multi-site operations, complex organizations with budgets of $10M+ or teams of 25+ employees.
California Health System Expertise:
Deep understanding of California's Medi-Cal ecosystem, Managed Care Plans (MCPs), reimbursement models, and evolving regulatory landscape.
Financial & Philanthropic Acumen:
Demonstrated financial leadership, including P&L oversight, unit economics, sustainable revenue strategy, payer contracting, and diversified funding models. We respond with research-informed programs that create connection, build resilience, and foster a true sense of belonging.
